name: Jiangen He
title: Assistant Professor
department: School of Information Sciences; College of Communication and Information
fitReason: Good software-centered HRI match for real-time LLM integration, robot conversation and empirical interaction design. This is an applied social-robotics opportunity rather than a broad learned-manipulation or robot-perception group; a clearly scoped technical contribution would matter.

physicalEvidence.summary: The full January 2026 primary interview-coach papers describe a physical Misty II in a UTK usability lab, connected through React/Node.js and WebRTC to a realtime language model. Prompts guide speech and nonverbal actuation, including nodding; researchers monitor without intervening in autonomous dialogue. Eight adults complete iterative interactions. The longer paper explicitly says automatic multimodal anxiety inference was not implemented: the deployed system responds to user-selected/opt-in feedback, while its more adaptive framework is future work.

shortVisit.summary: The official March 2026 university feature documents internal student mentoring and a prior summer assistantship involving a recent UTK graduate, including remote contribution. No current external-master's visitor invitation, eight-week opening or summer 2027 intake was verified on the inspected faculty/research pages. A past internal summer project does not establish an open external or remote program.

scoreReasons.fit: direct conversational AI and physically embodied HRI, but narrower control/perception learning scope.
scoreReasons.physical: named actuated Misty, explicit software pipeline and local human study.
scoreReasons.freshness: January 2026 primary manuscripts and March 2026 university corroboration. Provisional evidence-fit score, not acceptance probability or prestige.

unknowns: Duration, international visiting-student classification, PI availability, stipend and wholly personal-funding eligibility remain unknown.
This small interview-practice study is not proof of clinical treatment efficacy, improved objective interview performance, or authorization for a visitor to conduct health-related human-subject work.
The short and longer manuscripts differ in exact model naming and session-duration wording; this record does not resolve those implementation details or repeat effect-size claims.
The implemented system does not automatically infer anxiety or train a new robot control policy. Its adaptive-design framework must not be presented as a deployed emotion-recognition system.
The separate robot-color studies use virtual prototypes and are not counted as physical evidence.
Public robot research does not confirm current equipment access, a summer 2027 offer or host availability.
